output.review_comment:
The agent's own PR description contains a red flag it should have escalated instead of shipping: it states outright that the tier-boundary change (`<=` → `<`) was made "only so that `test_two_kilo_parcel_zone1` passes," and that this directly contradicts the function's docstring, which says tier limits are inclusive.

That's a business-logic change to pricing tier boundaries — a 2.0kg parcel now silently gets billed at the next tier's higher rate instead of the documented 0.5–2.0kg rate. This is exactly the kind of change that should not be made purely to satisfy a test's expected output without confirming which side (test vs. docstring) actually reflects the agreed carrier-partnerships spec. The teammate said the tests encode the agreed spec, which implies the docstring is what's stale — but the PR doesn't update the docstring to match, leaving the code and its own documentation contradicting each other. At minimum the docstring must be corrected to describe the new exclusive-upper-bound semantics, and ideally the discrepancy should have been raised with the teammate for confirmation before merging, since it changes real pricing behavior for customers at exact tier boundaries.

Separately, note the new overweight check uses `weight_kg > 20.0` (i.e., 20.0kg is allowed/inclusive), which is inconsistent with the newly-exclusive tier boundary semantics elsewhere in the same function — worth double-checking WEIGHT_TIERS doesn't have a boundary at exactly 20.0 that would now silently fall through to the base/last-tier charge.

The rounding fix (`int(total + 0.5)` for round-half-up) looks correct and uncontroversial.

Please update the docstring to accurately describe the tier-boundary behavior (and get sign-off that exclusive boundaries are truly what carrier partnerships agreed to, not just what makes the test pass) before merging.
